review_notes: Read the whole target file. Searched the repo and Mathlib for existing versions of the local helper concepts. Found a competing definition of the n-th q-coefficient linear functional on weight-k Gamma0 cusp forms: Definitions/Def_CuspForm_QCoeffLinear.lean has `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear M k n`, and the same local `qCoeffLin` is re-defined (with `_apply`) in at least six other Sol files. Not reported: local `pad` (similar to `PowerSeries.heckeV` / the library's `CuspForm.qCoeff_rescaleLin` formula, but it is a function-level d-scaled specialisation, so the case for consolidation is unclear); `hΓ` and `qCoeff_zero'` (theorem-level duplicates, excluded by the rubric); `RootsGood`, `L` (no Mathlib/library equivalent found). Remaining uncertainty: I did not check whether Def_CuspForm_QCoeffLinear is already transitively imported by the target (grep shows only two Thm files import it directly), but its own imports (Mathlib and Def_FLTPrelim_Modularity) are already imported by the target, so adding it is cheap.

findings.problem: The file defines its own linear functional 'n-th q-expansion coefficient' on CuspForm (Gamma0 M) 2, together with a rfl lemma `qCoeffLin_apply`. The library already has `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear M k n` with the same carrier, the same toFun, and the same linearity, for general weight k, and a lemma `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear_apply` with the same content. The weight-2 specialisation is therefore a second copy of the same concept. The file's only real use of it is in `qCoeff_zero'` and in `qCoeff_U_aeval_*` to turn map_add/map_sub/map_smul into qCoeff statements. The same local definition is also copy-pasted into several other Sol files (e.g. S_CuspForm_IsNewform_eq_of_forall_qCoeff_eq, S_CuspForm_IsNormalizedEigenform_qCoeff_eq_of_coprime_...), so the duplication spreads.
findings.proposed_change: Import Definitions.Def_CuspForm_QCoeffLinear and Theorems.Thm_CuspForm_qCoeffLinear_apply. Delete the local `qCoeffLin` and `qCoeffLin_apply`. Use `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear M 2 n` and `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear_apply` in `qCoeff_zero'` and in the `qCoeff_U_aeval_*` rewrites. The `hΓ` argument is not needed for this, because the library definition proves the analyticity hypotheses internally. Only the `rw [← qCoeffLin_apply, ...]` calls need renaming.
findings.benefit: One canonical q-coefficient linear map instead of a per-file copy. Linearity is proved once and no longer re-proved with local `hΓ` plumbing. The result is compatible with the library's other qCoeffLinear API. The file shrinks by about 14 lines.
